cwMessages.helpCut: cut numbers, t for 0 and n for 9: 599 is sent as 5nn

station.troubleshootingTitle: if the radio connects but shows no frequency
station.ft891Troubleshooting:
the radio is receiving commands but not responding. almost always one of:

- **cat rts off at the radio, or hold rts high on.** with **cat rts** on (ft-891 menu **05-08**), the radio stays silent while rts is low — it may answer once as the port opens, then nothing. picking the radio's own usb port turns on **hold rts high** under advanced settings. on a digirig, signalink or most home-brew cables rts is ptt, and holding it high keys your transmitter: turn cat rts off at the radio instead.
- **speed must match** the radio's cat rate (menu **05-06**). with a mismatch, the radio sends back garbage or nothing, and never an error.
- **another app may hold the port**: wsjt-x, fldigi and rigctld all keep it open.
station.yaesuBinaryTroubleshootingTitle: if the radio connects but shows no frequency
station.yaesuBinaryTroubleshooting:
this radio speaks yaesu's older five-byte cat, and it does not respond at all when something is off. almost always one of:

- **the cable must convert levels.** the cat jack on the back is not rs-232 and not usb; it needs a ct-62 or an equivalent adapter. a plain audio or data cable won't work for cat.
- **speed must match** the radio's cat rate menu (**#14** on an ft-817, **#19** on an ft-857 or ft-897). with a mismatch, the radio sends nothing back, and never an error.
- **never let anything raise rts or dtr on this port.** on most cables for these radios those lines are ptt and keying. an older interface powered from dtr is the exception: turn on **hold dtr high** under advanced settings for that one.
- **another app may hold the port**: wsjt-x, fldigi and rigctld all keep it open.

this driver was written from yaesu's published cat chart and has not been run against one of these radios. if it half-works, that is worth reporting.
station.tenTecTroubleshootingTitle: if the radio connects but shows no frequency
station.tenTecEagleTroubleshooting:
- **the usb-b port on the back is the cat link.** the radio shows up as a usb serial port; on windows it needs ten-tec's usb to uart driver, which appears in device manager as "usb to uart (comx)".
- **another app may hold the port**: wsjt-x, fldigi and rigctld all keep it open, and so does ten-tec's firmware updater.
- **setting the filter width from the app takes it away from the bw knob** until the radio is switched off and on again. that is how the radio works.

this driver was written from ten-tec's programmer's reference guide. if it half-works, that is worth reporting, with the firmware version from the radio's menu.
station.tenTecOrionTroubleshooting:
- **use a straight-through db-9 serial cable** to the serial data port, not a null-modem one.
- **this entry holds rts high**, because the orion uses rts and cts as its handshake. on an interface that keys ptt from rts, such as a digirig, turn off hold rts high under advanced settings, or the radio transmits as soon as the app connects.
- **cw from the app needs the radio's internal keyer on.** with it off, the radio ignores what the app sends.
- **another app may hold the port**: wsjt-x, fldigi and rigctld all keep it open.

this driver was written from ten-tec's programmer's reference guide and has not been run against an orion. if it half-works, that is worth reporting, with the firmware version from the radio's menu.
station.tenTecNoCw: this radio's firmware does not take cw from the app. ten-tec added it in orion firmware 1.366.
station.tenTecKeyerOff: the radio's internal keyer is off, so it ignores cw sent from the app. turn the keyer on in the radio's menu.
station.guohetecTroubleshootingTitle: if the radio connects but shows no frequency
station.guohetecTroubleshooting:
the q900 has two cat protocols, and this entry uses its native one rather than the ft-817 imitation. pick **guohetec q900** here, not an ft-817 — the imitation supports fewer commands, and the radio does not say which one it is using.

- **the usb-c cable is the cat link**, and it connects the sound card too. speed does not matter on it; the port ignores whatever it is set to.
- **never let anything raise rts or dtr on this port.** on a serial cable those lines are ptt and keying.
- **another app may hold the port**: wsjt-x, fldigi and rigctld all keep it open.
- **a second-generation radio behaves differently** from a first. long press menu, then about: hw 2.0 is the second generation.

this driver was written from the manufacturer's published protocol and has not been run against one of these radios. if it half-works, that is worth reporting.
station.yaesuTroubleshootingTitle: if the radio connects but shows no frequency
station.yaesuTroubleshooting:
the radio is receiving commands but not responding. almost always one of:

- **cat rts must be off at the radio.** with it on, the radio waits for a handshake line the app keeps low. on a digirig, signalink or most home-brew cables that same line is ptt, so raising it would key your transmitter. on the radio's own usb port, **hold rts high** under advanced settings is the alternative. where that setting lives differs by model (menu **05-08** on an ft-891).
- **speed must match** the radio's cat rate menu. with a mismatch, the radio sends back garbage or nothing, and never an error.
- **another app may hold the port**: wsjt-x, fldigi and rigctld all keep it open.
- **modes follow the ft-891's table.** most of the yaesu line matches it, but a radio that numbers its modes differently will show and set the wrong one for those. the frequency is unaffected.
station.yaesuRs232Troubleshooting:
the radio is receiving commands but not responding. almost always one of:

- **the cat jack is rs-232.** it needs a usb-to-serial adapter and a straight-through db-9 cable — a null-modem cable swaps the lines, and the radio never hears a thing.
- **cat rts must be off at the radio.** with it on, the radio waits for a handshake line the app keeps low unless **hold rts high** is on under advanced settings.
- **speed must match** the radio's cat rate menu. with a mismatch, the radio sends back garbage or nothing, and never an error.
- **another app may hold the port**: wsjt-x, fldigi and rigctld all keep it open.

this entry was written from published cat documentation and has not been run against one of these radios. if it half-works, that is worth reporting.
station.yaesuUsbTroubleshooting:
the radio is receiving commands but not responding. almost always one of:

- **use the first of the radio's two usb ports.** cat is normally on the first (the **enhanced** com port on windows); the second (**standard**) is for ptt and keying. the picker points at the first wherever it can tell the two apart.
- **cat rts off at the radio, or hold rts high on.** with the radio's **cat rts** menu on, it stays silent while rts is low — it may answer once as the port opens, then nothing. picking the radio's own usb port turns on **hold rts high** under advanced settings. on a digirig, signalink or most home-brew cables rts is ptt, and holding it high keys your transmitter: turn cat rts off at the radio instead.
- **speed must match** the radio's cat rate menu. with a mismatch, the radio sends back garbage or nothing, and never an error.
- **another app may hold the port**: wsjt-x, fldigi and rigctld all keep it open.
station.k4SerialNotes:
connect the k4’s rear usb-b (pc) socket. either usb-pc1 or usb-pc2 works for cat; choose an unused port and match its serial usb-pcn: baud rate setting on the radio. halo prefills 38400; change it if needed. another application must use the other port or ethernet.

this connection controls the radio and its keyers; it does not send audio to halo.
station.k4TcpNotes:
connect the k4’s ethernet socket to your local network. enter its hostname or ip address and cat port 9200. halo uses the same host on fixed port 9201 when a panadapter or waterfall is visible; changing the cat port does not change the spectrum port.

the spectrum shows the main receiver. its zoom, reference adjustment and speed controls affect only halo’s display. audio streaming is not supported.
station.k4PowerTimeout: k4 power was not changed because the radio did not confirm its output range. try again.
station.k4PowerRange: k4 power must be 0.1–110 w, or 0.0001–0.01 w when the transverter milliwatt output is active.
station.elecraftTroubleshootingTitle: if the radio connects but shows no frequency
station.elecraftTroubleshooting:
elecraft rigs speak kenwood cat, and a kx2 and a kx3 have both been run this way — vfo in both directions, mode switching and cw zero-beat all working.

if the radio does not respond, almost always one of:

- **speed must match** the rate set under **rs232** in the radio's menu. 38400 is what these ship on. with a mismatch, the radio sends back garbage or nothing, and never an error.
- **another app may hold the port**: wsjt-x, fldigi and rigctld all keep it open.

**if the frequency is right but the mode is wrong**, tell us. the kx2 and kx3 entries read the mode from a position in the radio's status reply that we have pinned from the rigs we have seen, and a firmware that puts it elsewhere is something only a report reaches us as.

the k3 has not been reported either way, so please say what happens if you run one. a k4 has its own entry.
station.lab599TroubleshootingTitle: if the radio connects but shows no frequency
station.lab599Troubleshooting:
the tx-500 line speaks kenwood cat. written from published references rather than tested on the radio, so please report what happens either way.

- **speed must match** the radio's cat setting, 9600 unless you changed it. with a mismatch the radio sends back garbage or nothing, and never an error.
- **pick the cat protocol on the radio.** ts-2000 covers frequency and mode. lab599 also lets the app switch the radio to dig.
- **through a link500mp**, press and hold the vfo knob for about three seconds to hand cat control to the interface.
- **over bluetooth on a computer**, the link500mp pairs as two serial ports and only one carries cat. if the radio stays silent, pick the other.
- **over bluetooth le**, as on an iphone or ipad, switch the link500mp to its ios mode first. in its other modes it does not show up in a scan.
station.kenwoodTroubleshootingTitle: if the radio connects but shows no frequency
station.kenwoodTroubleshooting:
this driver is proven against kenwood's ts-590sg and ts-480, qrp labs' qmx and qcx-mini, and elecraft's kx2 and kx3. the rest of the line is written from published cat references, so please report what happens either way.

if the radio does not respond, almost always one of:

- **speed must match** the radio's cat menu. with a mismatch, the radio sends back garbage or nothing, and never an error.
- **another app may hold the port**: wsjt-x, fldigi and rigctld all keep it open.
- **some rigs need cat enabled** in the menu before they respond at all.

**several sdr front-ends speak this same protocol**, so this entry is worth trying for those too; elecraft rigs are listed separately, under elecraft. if the frequency is right but the mode is wrong or missing, that is the one part that differs across the line — the app works it out from the radio and falls back to asking directly, so the mode may simply lag.
station.peerRadioElsewhereMessage: this radio is connected to ${device}. its connection and settings are configured on that device.
station.icomCivTroubleshootingTitle: if two serial ports show up for the same radio
station.icomCivTroubleshooting: several icom radios, the ic-705 among them, present **two** usb serial ports at once (icom calls them port a and port b), both set to ci-v by default. neither this app nor your os can tell them apart beyond that: the same usb vendor/product id just shows up twice, sometimes marked with a `#2` suffix here. **port a is usually the right one** — normally the first one your os or browser lists, and where this app can tell the two ports apart it marks that one as suggested. if commands go out and the radio never responds, try the other port next.
station.civAddressTroubleshooting:
- **the ci-v address must match** the radio's menu. this entry prefills the address the model ships with, but a rig sharing a ci-v bus is exactly where that gets changed. a frame sent to the wrong address is ignored in silence, which looks exactly like a dead cable.
- **speed must match** the radio's ci-v baud rate (on usb, ci-v usb baud rate). set the radio to the same number shown here, **not auto**. on auto some radios, the ic-7300 among them, connect and then stop responding after a minute or so.
- **another app may hold the port**: wsjt-x, fldigi and rigctld all keep it open.
station.icomUsbSpeedFollows: - **there is no speed to set.** over usb this radio talks at whatever speed the computer uses, and this entry always uses 115200, the speed the scope needs.
station.ic7610UsbSpeed: - **set ci-v usb baud rate to 115200**, the speed this entry always uses, since the scope needs it — **not auto**. a radio set to any other speed answers with silence.
station.ic7300Mk2Note: - the **ic-7300 mk2** ships on address `B6`, not the `94` prefilled here — pick the ic-7300 mk2 entry instead.
station.ic705PortNote: - the **ic-705** presents two usb serial ports, both named after the radio. ci-v is on the **first** of them, which the picker points at wherever it can tell the two apart.
station.ic7760PortNote: - the **ic-7760** speaks ci-v on **port a** of the two usb serial ports it presents.
station.x6100PortNote: - the **x6100** speaks ci-v on its **dev** port — the second of the two serial ports it presents, and the one the picker points at.
station.rigctldTroubleshooting:
this connects to a **rigctld daemon you run yourself**, not to the radio directly — hamlib's backend talks to the radio and supports hundreds of models.

- **the daemon must already be running**, e.g. `rigctld -m 1035 -r /dev/ttyUSB0`. find your radio's model number with `rigctl -l`.
- **from another machine**, start it with `-T 0.0.0.0`: by default rigctld only accepts connections from the machine it runs on.
- **port** is 4532 unless you started the daemon with `-t`.
- once connected, a missing frequency usually means the daemon itself cannot reach the radio. test it with `rigctl -m 2 f` on the daemon's machine.
station.flrigTroubleshooting:
this connects to an **flrig program you run yourself**, not to the radio directly — flrig talks to the radio and supports most makes and models.

- **flrig must already be running**, with its transceiver configured and connected.
- **port** is 12345 unless you changed it in flrig's configuration (config → setup → server).
- **from another machine**, make sure flrig's server is reachable. it listens on all interfaces, but your firewall may not agree.
- once connected, a missing frequency usually means flrig itself cannot reach the radio. check that flrig's display is following the dial.
station.hrdTroubleshooting:
this connects to **ham radio deluxe's rig control, running on your computer**, not to the radio directly — hrd talks to the radio.

- **rig control must already be running** and connected to the radio.
- **its ip server must be enabled.** rig control only talks to other programs through it.
- **port** is 7809 unless you changed it in the ip server's settings.
- **from another machine**, make sure your firewall lets the connection through.

this entry was written from published descriptions of hrd's protocol and has not been run against hrd. if it half-works, that is worth reporting.
station.n3fjpTroubleshooting:
this connects to **an n3fjp logging program running on your computer**, not to the radio directly — n3fjp talks to the radio.

- **the program's api must be on**: settings → application program interface, check **tcp api enabled**.
- **port** is 1100 unless you changed it there.
- **n3fjp must have a radio interface set up** to follow or tune the radio. without one, it reports only what is typed into its entry window.
- n3fjp reports band, mode and frequency only: no power, no transmit state.

this entry was written from n3fjp's published api and has not been run against n3fjp. if it half-works, that is worth reporting.
station.commanderTroubleshooting:
this connects to **dxlab commander, running on your computer**, not to the radio directly — commander talks to the radio.

- **commander must already be running** and connected to the radio.
- **its network service must be on**: the **net serv** button in the radio panel of commander's configuration window.
- **port** is 52002, the third port of the block starting at net serv's **base port** (52000 unless you changed it).
- **from another machine**, make sure your firewall lets the connection through.

this entry was written from commander's published tcp messages and has not been run against commander. if it half-works, that is worth reporting.
station.ic705Troubleshooting:
the radio has a **single** remote-control session. when the login is ignored, something else is almost always using it.

- **close any other client.** wfview or rs-ba1 connected to the same radio holds that one session, and the login here is simply ignored while it does.
- **check the radio's network settings.** wlan must be on, the radio must be on the same network, and its remote-control (network) function must be enabled.
- **the ports must match** the radio's control port and serial port (udp), or the ports forwarded to them. a wrong port is met with silence, the same as a radio that is off.
- **power-cycle the radio's wlan** if it stays stuck. that reliably clears a session stuck on the radio.

a **wrong password is refused explicitly**, not met with silence. if you got here rather than a "rejected" message, the password is not the problem.
station.icomLanTroubleshooting:
the radio has a **single** remote-control session. when the login is ignored, something else is almost always using it.

- **close any other client.** wfview, rs-ba1 or icom's remote utility connected to the same radio holds that one session, and the login here is simply ignored while it does.
- **check the radio's network settings.** its lan port must be connected to the same network as this device, its **network control** must be on, and the username and password must be set up as a network user on the radio.
- **the ports must match** the radio's control port and serial port (udp), or the ports forwarded to them. a wrong port is met with silence, the same as a radio that is off.
- **if it connects but never answers**, the ci-v address here must match the radio's ci-v address menu. this entry prefills the address the model ships with.
- **turn the radio off and on** if it stays stuck.
